text:
charlie-support: FYI customer reported a run of 503s from CloudHSM during their DR failover window. They see TLS handshake failures and missing audit events for ~3h. Also weirdly their billing shows a short spike during the same timeframe. Escalating — can someone take a look? @anna-security

mike-infra: Can you paste the client-side error and a couple of server logs? 503 + handshake usually means session/socket teardown or cert mismatch.

charlie-support: Here's the snippet customer sent from the app logs: `2026-05-12T11:02:06Z sign_request failed: tls: handshake failure` and from our gateway: 
```
upstream hsm-usw2 error: EOF during handshake
conn_id=2345 session_reset=true
```. They also attached a CloudHSM diag but I haven't parsed it.

anna-security: Important — they said audit events (sign/verify) are absent for 11:00–14:00 UTC. That window overlaps the billing spike. Could be key ownership change or audit proxy outage. @vendor-cloudhsm can you check if any cluster-level rekey/maintenance happened? :eyes:

vendor-cloudhsm: Confirming we have a maintenance event for cluster c-abc123 at 11:05 UTC — short restart of one HSM node for cert rotation. No planned rekey. We saw a transient TLS renegotiation storm afterwards (connections reopened). Monitoring shows session_count jumped ~4x for ~6m.

hsm-bot: ALERT: cluster c-abc123 us-west-2 - session_count spike to 4200 (baseline 1100) at 2026-05-12T11:06:12Z. error_rate_sign=2.8% -> peaked 12.1% for 7m.

jess-ops: If they were failing over clients at the same time, we could have thundering herd on reconnect that exceeds HSM session limits or overwhelms TLS handshake concurrency. Ask customer if they retried aggressively. Also need pcap of TLS failures and their client connection pool settings.

charlie-support: Customer confirms they retried with backoff 0-200ms (not exponential) and concurrent processes ~300. They use a short-lived connection per request pattern.

tom-eng: That pattern + node restart = session storm. Two quick mitigation options: 1) enable connection pooling on client side (recommended) 2) enable our software fallback signer for critical paths while vendor fixes cluster (temporary). Also we should check KMS key handle stability — if key material was migrated the API might reject older sessions.

anna-security: We need audit integrity proof for compliance. Ask vendor for signed timeline of node restart and evidence there was no key export or rewrap. Also request missing audit records — if vendor retained them we can ingest.

mike-infra: Repro steps for internal triage:
1) run openssl verify against HSM endpoint: `openssl s_client -connect hsm-usw2.example:8443 -tls1_2 -brief`
2) tail gateway logs with filter: `grep "handshake failure\|session_reset" /var/log/redwood/gateway.log`
3) compare CloudHSM metrics: `aws cloudhsmv2 get-metric-data --metric-names SessionCount,SignErrors --start 2026-05-12T10:50:00Z --end 2026-05-12T14:30:00Z`

charlie-support: Customer provided pcap showing repeated `ClientHello` and immediate `RST` from our side after `Alert: handshake failure`. Uploading to secure bucket and shared with infra.

vendor-cloudhsm: We've pulled audit logs and there was a gap in delivery to our analytics pipeline caused by the node restart — raw audit entries exist on-device for the window. We'll provide signed export and a vendor-signed attestation by EOD. No key material was exported or rewrapped.

jess-ops: Short-term mitigation for affected tenants: enable `REDWOOD_FALLBACK_SIGNER=on` for their routes, add jittered backoff + max concurrency cap (e.g., 50) on client. Long-term: enforce connection pooling or use persistent sessions via our SDK.

tom-eng: Also adding a server-side guard to limit handshake concurrency per HSM endpoint in the gateway (throttle new handshakes when session_count > 85% of capacity). I'll open PR and a canary.

charlie-support: Customer accepted fallback signer and reduced concurrency. Errors dropped to baseline within 10m. They've requested a compliance artifact for the audit gap.

anna-security: OK — track vendor attestation + postmortem. Assigning to incident-ops for final report and compliance packet. :thumbsup:

mike-infra: Filing follow-up ticket: #INC-2026-1834 — include pcap, gateway logs, vendor attestation, billing spike query.

charlie-support: Thanks everyone — ping me when postmortem and signed audit bundle are in.

vendor-cloudhsm: Attestation uploaded to shared folder: `s3://redwood-support/attachments/1769954321/vendor-attestation.pdf` (signed).

jess-ops: Noted. Scheduling postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 UTC with infra + security + vendor reps. :calendar:
